questions.question: A patient has a mass obstructing the left interventricular foramen of Monro. Which ventricular compartment is expected to enlarge first?
questions.explanation: Obstruction of the left foramen of Monro traps CSF in the left lateral ventricle.

questions.question: A child has narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct. MRI shows ventricular enlargement above the obstruction. Which pattern is most likely?
options: Enlarged lateral and third ventricles with a relatively normal fourth ventricle
Enlarged third and fourth ventricles with normal lateral ventricles
questions.explanation: Aqueduct obstruction enlarges the upstream lateral and third ventricles; the fourth lies downstream.

questions.question: A patient has obstruction of both lateral apertures and the median aperture of the fourth ventricle. CSF is prevented from flowing directly into which compartment?
questions.explanation: The fourth ventricular apertures allow CSF to enter the subarachnoid space.

questions.question: During surgery, the median outlet of the fourth ventricle is identified. What is its name?
questions.explanation: Magendie is the median aperture of the fourth ventricle.

questions.question: A lesion blocks the outlet at the lateral end of a fourth ventricular lateral recess. Which opening is affected?
questions.explanation: The paired foramina of Luschka are the lateral apertures.

questions.question: A tracer is introduced into a lateral ventricle. Which sequence describes its normal route toward the subarachnoid space?
options: Monro → third ventricle → aqueduct → fourth ventricle → Magendie/Luschka
Aqueduct → third ventricle → Monro → fourth ventricle → Magendie/Luschka
Monro → fourth ventricle → aqueduct → third ventricle → Magendie/Luschka
Magendie → third ventricle → aqueduct → fourth ventricle → Monro
questions.explanation: CSF passes through Monro, the third ventricle, the aqueduct, and the fourth ventricular outlets.

questions.question: Following meningitis, a patient develops scarring that impairs CSF absorption, although the ventricular pathways remain patent. Which structures are most directly affected?
questions.explanation: Impaired absorption at arachnoid villi can cause communicating hydrocephalus.

questions.question: A student follows CSF absorption from the subarachnoid space through arachnoid granulations. Into which structure does much of this CSF drain?
questions.explanation: Arachnoid granulations drain CSF into dural venous sinuses, especially the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.question: A patient develops increased dural venous sinus pressure. How can this interfere with CSF absorption through arachnoid villi?
options: It directly blocks the foramina of Monro
It stops CSF production by all choroid plexuses
It reduces the pressure gradient driving CSF into venous blood
It forces all CSF into the spinal central canal
questions.explanation: Absorption depends on CSF pressure exceeding venous sinus pressure.

questions.question: A ventricular tumor arises from the tissue responsible for producing most CSF. Which tissue is involved?
questions.explanation: Choroid plexuses produce most CSF, principally within the lateral ventricles.
